purpose: Pipeline 1-6 pilot for SPA Things to do cards only. This file does not publish or generate Field Cards.

activities.name: Don Khon & Old Railway Bridge
facts: The historic railway bridge connects Don Det with Don Khon and opens the island route beyond Don Det.
The bridge is reached south from Don Det on foot or by bicycle.
Allow around half a day when the bridge is combined with a relaxed Don Khon loop.
The bridge route itself has no mandatory activity fee; individual sights and services on Don Khon may charge separately.
Early morning is cooler for walking or cycling the island road.

draft.shortDescription: Cross the old railway bridge from Don Det into Don Khon, where bicycles, village paths and traces of the former Mekong portage railway shape the route.
draft.gettingThere: Bicycle or walk · south from Don Det

photoCandidates.alt: The historic bridge connecting Don Det and Don Khon in Si Phan Don
photoCandidates.author: Dominic Nelson

activities.name: Li Phi · Somphamit Waterfalls
facts: Somphamit is the developed Don Khon waterfall area commonly called Li Phi, where the Mekong breaks through broad rock channels.
From Don Det, cycle across the old bridge to Don Khon and continue to the signed waterfall park.
Allow around 1.5 to 3 hours for the waterfall viewpoints and paths.
The waterfall park has a mandatory entrance fee, while optional activities cost extra.
Early morning gives cooler cycling conditions before the exposed island roads heat up.

draft.shortDescription: Cycle across Don Khon to Somphamit, where the Mekong tears through wide rock channels and a sequence of viewpoints reveals the scale of Li Phi.

photoCandidates.alt: Li Phi and Somphamit rapids on Don Khon in Si Phan Don
photoCandidates.author: Basile Morin

activities.name: Khone Phapheng Falls
facts: Khone Phapheng is the immense Mekong cataract south of Don Det near the Cambodian border.
From Don Det, travel by boat to Nakasang and continue by road to the waterfall area.
Treat the outing as a half-day trip from Don Det.
The developed waterfall site has a mandatory entrance fee.
Morning is a practical time for the boat and road transfer from Don Det.

draft.shortDescription: Leave Don Det for Khone Phapheng, where the Mekong spreads into an immense cataract and the journey combines an island boat crossing with a road transfer.
draft.gettingThere: Boat to Nakasang · then road transfer

activities.name: Don Som
facts: Don Som is a quieter inhabited agricultural island north of Don Det, with village roads and farming landscapes rather than packaged attractions.
Reach Don Som by local boat from Don Det and arrange the return before the boat leaves.
A half-day works for a short visit, while a full day suits slower cycling.
The local boat crossing requires a fare, with bicycles potentially costing extra.
Morning leaves enough daylight to explore and arrange a predictable return boat.

draft.shortDescription: Cross by local boat to Don Som, a quieter farming island where village roads, fields and ordinary Mekong life replace Don Det’s traveller strip.
draft.gettingThere: Local boat · from Don Det pier

activities.name: Khone Pa Soi Waterfall
facts: Khone Pa Soi is a smaller waterfall route on the eastern side of Don Khon, reached by rougher island tracks.
Cycle across the Don Det to Don Khon bridge and continue toward the eastern side of Don Khon.
Allow around 1 to 2 hours for the waterfall area.
No dependable mandatory entrance fee is verified, so the activity is treated as free while visitors should carry small cash for possible local contributions.
Morning gives cooler conditions and more daylight for the rougher cycling route.

draft.shortDescription: Follow Don Khon’s rougher eastern tracks to Khone Pa Soi, a smaller Mekong waterfall route where the quieter bicycle approach is part of the experience.

activities.name: Xai Kong Nyai Beach
facts: Xai Kong Nyai is a sandy Mekong beach on Don Khon with simple food stops and local long-tail boats.
Reach Don Khon by the old railway bridge and continue downstream from the Somphamit area by bicycle or on foot.
Keep around 1 to 3 hours for food, rest and a cautious swim close to shore.
Beach access is generally free; food and optional boat trips cost extra.
Afternoon works naturally as a slower stop after visiting Somphamit.

draft.shortDescription: Continue beyond Somphamit to Xai Kong Nyai, a sandy Don Khon riverbank for simple food, a slow rest and cautious swimming close to shore.

photoCandidates.alt: Sandy Mekong beach on Don Khon
photoCandidates.author: Basile Morin

activities.name: Si Phan Don by Boat
facts: Local long-tail boats can be chartered from Don Det for flexible trips through the wider Si Phan Don channels and islands.
Arrange the route, duration, price and return directly with a local boat driver at Don Det.
A custom trip can run from half a day to a full day depending on the route.
A private or shared local boat trip requires an agreed fare.
Morning leaves the widest daylight window for a flexible island route.

draft.shortDescription: Charter a local long-tail boat from Don Det and follow the Mekong beyond the main islands through working channels, village banks and quieter Si Phan Don scenery.
draft.gettingThere: Arrange locally · Don Det boat pier

activities.name: 4,000 Islands Kayaking
facts: Guided kayaking from Don Det uses the southern Si Phan Don channels and may combine paddling, short overland sections and waterfall stops.
Join an organised kayak trip from Don Det rather than attempting the stronger river sections independently.
The standard river excursion is treated as a full-day activity.
The guided kayak trip requires a paid tour package.
Morning is the normal start for a full-day river itinerary.

draft.shortDescription: Paddle the southern Si Phan Don channels on a guided day from Don Det, mixing calm water, stronger current and short overland sections between river stops.

activities.name: Cycle Don Det & Don Khon
facts: Don Det and Don Khon are commonly explored by bicycle along mostly flat island roads and paths linked by the old railway bridge.
Rent a bicycle on Don Det and start directly from the village paths.
Allow half a day for a focused loop or a full day when adding waterfalls and slower stops.
A rental bicycle requires a daily fee for travellers without their own bicycle.
Early morning is cooler for the exposed island roads.

draft.shortDescription: Rent a bicycle on Don Det and link flat island paths, the old railway bridge and Don Khon’s quieter roads into an easy self-paced day.
draft.gettingThere: Start on Don Det · rental bicycle

activities.name: Tubing on Don Det
facts: Tubing remains a Don Det river activity, using a rented inner tube on suitable Mekong sections when local conditions allow.
Arrange the tube and current local route guidance on Don Det before entering the river.
Keep roughly 1 to 3 hours for a tubing session rather than treating it as a full-day excursion.
A tube rental is required and therefore the activity has a participation cost.
Afternoon is a common relaxed window, subject to current, weather and local advice.

draft.shortDescription: Rent a tube on Don Det and float a suitable Mekong section at river pace, checking the current route and conditions locally before entering the water.

activities.name: Sunset on Don Det
facts: The western side of Don Det opens toward Mekong sunset views across the channels and low island horizon.
Walk or cycle to the western side of Don Det before the light begins to drop.
Allow around 1 to 2 hours for an unhurried walk, drink or riverside stop around sunset.
Watching sunset from the public island roads and riverbank has no mandatory participation fee.
Sunset is the defining time for the experience.

draft.shortDescription: Walk or cycle to Don Det’s western side as the light drops across the Mekong, then stay for an unhurried riverside end to the day.
draft.gettingThere: Walk or bicycle · west Don Det
